newsitem.title: USA: Intel sees gigabyte internal PC bandwidth.
newsitem.headline: Intel sees gigabyte internal PC bandwidth.

text.p: A senior Intel Corp executive said the company expects personal computers to deliver one gigabyte per second internal bandwidth capabilities by the year 2000.

Albert Yu, senior vice president of Intel's Microprocessor Products Group, said the company is working on a 4X version of its Accelerated Graphics Port that will deliver internal bandwidth in the one gigabyte range. Intel's 1X and 2X AGP, already well underway, are set to deliver 256 megabyte and 526 megabyte per second performance respectively -- roughly two and four times the current PCI bus's rating of 133 megabytes.
Yu noted that industry support for AGP technology has enabled AGP products to go from design to retail availability in less than one year.

Yu said in a presentation to an Intel visual computing conference here that Intel was also looking at boosting floating point performance in addition to adding faster memory capabilities to personal computers.
ATI Technologies Inc, 3Dlabs Inc Ltd, Cirrus Logic Inc, Evans & Sutherland Computer Corp and S3 Inc, among others, said they will be shipping AGP-enabled products in 1997.

The new 4X AGP enhancement, initially primarily targeted at high-end workstations and other high-performance platforms, will be incorporated into the AGP specifications in the fourth quarter of 1997, Intel said.

Moshe Dunie, Microsoft Corp's vice president of Windows operating systems, said the performance increases are critical for improving PC performance. "The bandwidth technology requirement will be increasing significantly," he said, noting that the PCI bus actually operates effectively at lower levels than its rated performance -- closer to 50 megabytes per second rather than its 133 megabyte rating.
He said he expects AGP devices will operate much more closely to their performance ratings, however.
